scorecard.rationale: The 21-person whole dried Ajwa crossover reported near-identical abdominal pain diary means, and the pediatric whole-date and mouse comparisons did not clearly separate groups. Date syrups had favorable labor-pain observations with preparation, comparator and population limits. The 34-person date-seed exercise trial reported lower pain at 24 hours (3.35 vs 5.00 on a 0–10 scale, p<.001), with an inconclusive immediate contrast. Its companion biomarkers belong to the same cohort. Parkinson bar studies supply whole-product or composite outcomes without an attributable date-paste and pain comparison. Separate public accounts recall less abdominal pain or more discomfort after date fruit, without an established Parkinson diagnosis or controlled exposure. Extract results are confounded by sedation. No observed study direction transfers defensibly to whole dried-date intake and pain severity in Parkinson disease. The fresh Rutab trial pooled 76 labor-pain categories across arms, and the late-pregnancy whole-fruit comparison reports labor progression without a pain score. Two favorable syrup trials are independent of each other, while the two Khorramabad reports share participants. The later review could not pool a pain estimate. Spanish ethnobotanical and historical sources document intended fruit analgesia and postpartum use without observed patient change or known drying state. None of these sources supplies enough transfer for a dried-date effect on Parkinson pain.
